newsitem.title: USA: Lawmakers still differ widely on bank reform-Leach.
newsitem.headline: Lawmakers still differ widely on bank reform-Leach.

text.p: Members of the House Banking Committee are generally in favor of overhauling U.S. financial sector laws, but important differences are yet to be resolved, committee chairman Jim Leach said Wednesday.

"It appears there is general consensus among committee members to move forward this session with financial modernization legislation, which would allow the affiliation of banks with insurance and securities firms," the Iowa Republican said at the beginning of a hearing on bank reform proposals here.
Leach said lawmakers still differ "on how best to regulate this new financial structure and whether the affiliation rights of banks should be expanded to include industrial interests."
Leach said he had wanted to include Secretary of the Treasury Robert Rubin at Wednesday's hearing, but said Rubin was not ready yet.

"We have received a request that treasury's testimony be delayed until June 3," Leach said. "We will honor that request, but members should be advised that it remains my intention to move to a committee markup in early June and to take a bill to the floor this summer."
